metaDesc: A day-by-day Nan temple and culture itinerary covering Wat Phumin, Phra That Chae Haeng, the Nan National Museum and the Tai Lue temples of Tha Wang Pha, with opening hours, fees and honest tips.
keywords: Nan temples, Wat Phumin, Phra That Chae Haeng, Nan National Museum, Wat Nong Bua Tai Lue, Nan itinerary
h1:
Nan Temples & Culture
2 Days: Phumin · Chae Haeng · Tai Lue
intro: Nan is the kind of town where you can spend a whole day temple-hopping and never get bored, because the temples here aren't just ordinary ordination halls. They come with wall murals, Tai Lue architecture and Lanna stories you won't easily find elsewhere. We've laid out a relaxed two-day route, from Wat Phumin in the centre of town with its famous "Pu Man Ya Man" whispering-lovers mural, out to Phra That Chae Haeng, the temple at the heart of Nan's identity, and across to see real Tai Lue temples in Tha Wang Pha district.

blocks.html: If you had to pick one theme for a Nan trip that really captures the town, temples and culture is the answer. The old town of Nan packs several temples within walking distance of each other, and most of them are free to enter, open 6am to 6pm. We've set up day one to cover the in-town sights plus Phra That Chae Haeng across the river in Phu Phiang, and day two to drive north to the Tai Lue temples around Tha Wang Pha. If you have a car or rent a motorbike, you'll get around far more easily.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Nan Old Town + Phra That Chae Haeng

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Old town · museum · Phra That Chae Haeng

items.activity: Wat Phumin — see the "Pu Man Ya Man" mural
items.note: A temple right in the middle of town, open 6am–6pm, free. The cruciform ordination hall is wrapped by twin nagas, and the famous whispering-lovers mural is on the inner wall, painted by Nan Bua Phan, a Tai Lue artisan. Go early when it's quiet and easy to photograph.

items.activity: Nan National Museum — the Black Ivory Tusk
items.note: Right across from Wat Phumin, an easy walk. Open Wed–Sun 9am–4pm (closed Mon–Tue). Admission 20 THB for Thais, 100 THB for foreigners. The building itself was the former palace hall of Nan's rulers.

items.activity: Stroll the frangipani-arched museum street + lunch
items.note: The road in front of the museum has a tunnel of arching frangipani trees that photographs beautifully. There are khao soi and Ngiao-style noodle shops around here to stop at.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Chae Haeng — the Year of the Rabbit stupa
items.note: In Phu Phiang district, about 3 km from town, open 6am–6pm, free. The golden stupa is clad in jangko gold sheeting and gleams. It's the temple at the heart of Nan's identity and the birth-year stupa for people born in the Year of the Rabbit.

items.activity: Wat Phra That Khao Noi — sunset view over Nan
items.note: Up on a hill on the west side, with a terrace around the Phra Phutta Maha Udom Mongkol Nanthaburi Si Nan Buddha image that looks out over the whole town. Open until 6pm, and you can drive all the way to the top. It's the best spot in town to catch the evening light.

blocks.title: Sequence it right
blocks.html: The Nan National Museum is closed Monday and Tuesday. If your trip lands on those two days, do Wat Phumin and Phra That Chae Haeng first and save the museum for a day when it's open.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Tai Lue Temples of Tha Wang Pha

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Drive north to Tha Wang Pha · the real Tai Lue murals

items.activity: Leave Nan town and head north to Tha Wang Pha district
items.note: About 40 km, roughly a 50-min drive. The road is smooth and runs past rice fields and villages, so it's a nice early-morning drive.

items.activity: Wat Nong Bua — the viharn and Tai Lue murals
items.note: The old Tai Lue viharn dates to around 1862. The inner walls carry murals telling the Chanthakhat Jataka, woven through with Tai Lue daily life, steamships and French soldiers. It's one of the most complete Tai Lue murals in Nan.

items.activity: Walk Nong Bua Tai Lue village — flowing-water weaving
items.note: The community around the temple still weaves and sells the "flowing-water" (lai nam lai) pattern cloth, which makes a good souvenir. Scarves start in the low hundreds of THB; larger pieces with finer patterns run into the thousands.

items.activity: Local lunch around Tha Wang Pha, then Wat Ton Laeng
items.note: Wat Ton Laeng is another old Tai Lue temple, with the low, tiered viharn roof typical of traditional Tai Lue style. It's quieter than Nong Bua, with a calm, peaceful feel.

items.activity: Drive back to Nan and catch the in-town temples you missed
items.note: If you still have energy, stop at Wat Ming Muang (a white ordination hall covered in stucco patterns) or Wat Si Phan Ton (a golden viharn with green nagas) in town before heading back to your hotel.

blocks.text: Reading the murals so they're more fun

blocks.html: Nan's wall murals are fun because they don't only depict religious scenes. They quietly record everyday life of the period everywhere you look. At Wat Phumin, the "Pu Man Ya Man" mural shows a man and woman whispering to each other. He's a young Man (Burmese) man, she's a Tai Lue woman, which you can tell from their dress and hairstyles. It was painted around 1867–1874 during a restoration of the temple.

items: Wat Phumin — look for the Pu Man Ya Man mural on the inner wall, and notice the pair of nagas threading through the cruciform ordination hall.
Wat Nong Bua — spot the steamship and the French soldiers tucked into the Jataka scenes, reflecting the colonial era.
The Black Ivory Tusk in the museum — a dark-brown left tusk, 97 cm long and 18 kg, a treasure of Nan you shouldn't skip.

items.name: Wat Ming Muang
items.blurb: An all-white ordination hall covered in stucco patterns, in the centre of town near the city pillar. Walkable from Wat Phumin.

items.name: Wat Si Phan Ton
items.blurb: A golden viharn with green nagas slithering down the stairs, very photogenic. Many people pair it with a visit to Wat Phumin.

items.name: Hoh Sin Rim Nan Gallery
items.blurb: A contemporary art gallery on the bank of the Nan River, a nice break from temples with a chilled-out cafe to sit in.

faq.q: Do you have to pay to visit the temples in Nan?
faq.a: Most temples in Nan, such as Wat Phumin, Phra That Chae Haeng and Wat Phra That Khao Noi, are free to enter and open roughly 6am–6pm. The one with an admission fee is the Nan National Museum: 20 THB for Thais, 100 THB for foreigners.

faq.q: What days is the Nan National Museum open?
faq.a: It's open Wednesday to Sunday, 9am–4pm, and closed Monday and Tuesday. If your trip lands on the two closed days, do the other temples first and come back on a day the museum is open.

faq.q: Where are the Tai Lue temples worth seeing for the murals?
faq.a: Wat Nong Bua in Tha Wang Pha district, about 40 km from Nan town, is one of the most complete Tai Lue wall murals around. Nearby is Wat Ton Laeng, another old example of Tai Lue architecture.

faq.q: Do you need a car for a Nan temple trip?
faq.a: Several old-town temples are within walking distance of each other, but Phra That Chae Haeng, Wat Phra That Khao Noi and the Tai Lue temples in Tha Wang Pha are out of town. A car or a rented motorbike is by far the most convenient, since public transport in Nan is limited.

faq.q: Which birth year is Phra That Chae Haeng the stupa for?
faq.a: Phra That Chae Haeng is the birth-year stupa for the Year of the Rabbit. People born in that year often come to pay respects, and it's also the temple at the heart of Nan's identity that almost everyone stops by when visiting.
